acquisition_method.value: data dependent selection of the top 10 precursors
acquisition_method.evidence: The data‐dependent selection of the top 10 precursors selected from a mass range of m/z 300–1600 was used for data acquisition, which consisted of a 70,000‐resolution full‐scan MS scan at m/z 200 (AGC set to 1e6 ions with a maximum fill time of 250 ms).

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Iodoacetamide (15 mM final concentration) was added, and samples were incubated protected from light for 30 mins with mixing.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Iodoacetamide (15 mM final concentration) was added, and samples were incubated protected from light for 30 mins with mixing.

cleavage_agent.evidence: The enzyme specificity was trypsin with 2 allowed missed cleavages, carbamidomethylation of cysteine (fixed modification) and oxidation of methionine (variable modification), m/z error tolerances of 10 ppm for peptide ions and 20 ppm for fragment ion spectra were used.

Beads were washed 3 times in acetonitrile (ACN) and 3 times in absolute ethanol prior to on-bead digestion in 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate and trypsin (1:50 enzyme to protein ratio) at 37°C for 2 hours with mixing.

collision_energy.evidence: MS/MS data were acquired using quadrupole ion selection with a 3.0 m/z window, HCD fragmentation with a normalized collision energy of 30 and in the orbitrap analyzer at 17,500‐resolution at m/z 250 (AGC target 5e4 ion with a maximum fill time of 250 ms).

enrichment_method.evidence: Magnetic affinity-based isolation was used to enrich the membrane particle fraction using a bead based protocol developed by Wu et al (Wu et al., 2023).

fragmentation_method.evidence: MS/MS data were acquired using quadrupole ion selection with a 3.0 m/z window, HCD fragmentation with a normalized collision energy of 30 and in the orbitrap analyzer at 17,500‐resolution at m/z 250 (AGC target 5e4 ion with a maximum fill time of 250 ms).
